title: Lab-Grown Meat (Awareness Level)
desc: Understand how cultivated meat is made, what it means for safety, nutrition, ethics, jobs and the environment, and how to read claims.
outcomes: Explain the steps of cell-cultivated meat in plain words.
Compare it with farmed and plant-based protein.
Check claims about environment and cost.
Draft a balanced one-page fact sheet.
task: Write a balanced one-page fact sheet on cultivated meat, with a comparison table and a claim checker.
condition: A computer, public information, two peers and a mentor. No production or sales is planned.
standard: Facts sourced and dated; benefits and unknowns both stated; approval status per place is named; no promotion; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Students, food entrepreneurs, journalists, policy staff, curious consumers.
evidence: fact sheet, comparison table, claim checker
modules: Real animal cells grown in a vessel.
A small sample is taken; cells multiply in nutrients.
Scaffolds give shape; cells mature into tissue.
It is different from plant-based meat.
A bioreactor grows cells for several weeks into a patty.
Cell line, growth medium, bioreactor, harvest, forming, cooking.
Growth medium once used animal serum; newer media avoid it.
A pilot plant changes to a serum-free medium.
Regulators review cell source, medium, process and allergens.
Only a few places have approved sales.
A regulator approves one product after reviewing safety data.
List approval status for your place.
Taste depends on fat and texture.
A table shows similar protein but different fat.
Energy use and land use vary.
Compare land, water and emissions per kg.
Energy mix of the factory changes results.
Results vary widely between studies; a fact sheet states a range.
Animal welfare, religion and food culture views differ.
A community panel discusses halal and vegetarian views.
Write two paragraphs on two views.
Cell biology technicians, process operators, food safety, quality, regulatory.
Skills from food and brewing carry across.
A brewery technician moves to a bioprocess role.
Readers state three facts and two unknowns.
quiz: Real animal cells grown in a vessel.
Cell line, growth medium, bioreactor, harvest.
Animal welfare, religion or farmers' livelihood.
Be clear about what it is.
rubric: Every claim linked to a dated record and checked by a peer
Checked, dated and explained to others
next: alternative protein food products, food industry, greenhouse gas auditing.
local: Approval and labelling of cultivated meat differ by place.
ladder: L1: learner can say what it is.
L4: learner can check approval status.
L6: learner can lead a briefing.
L7: learner can audit a fact sheet.
